title: Sanitation Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.141)
subtitle: Use on a walk-through of housekeeping, water supply, toilets, washrooms and eating areas at a permanent workplace.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A, and note the location of each defect.
When an item fails, record it, assign someone to correct it and recheck it before closing it out.
Manufacturer's instructions for fixtures and dispensers, other OSHA standards and site rules may add checks.

sections.title: Housekeeping, waste and vermin
items: Work areas are clean as far as the work allows, with no avoidable buildup of dirt or debris.
Floors are dry where practicable; wet-process areas have working drainage and mats, platforms or false floors, or waterproof footgear is provided.
No protruding nails, splinters, loose boards, or unnecessary holes and openings in floors, working places or passageways.
Receptacles for putrescible waste do not leak and can be thoroughly cleaned.
Each putrescible-waste receptacle has a lid that is solid and fits tightly, unless it stays sanitary without one.
Sweepings, refuse and garbage are removed often enough that the area stays sanitary and no waste creates a health menace.
No signs of rodents or insects; openings and spaces that would let vermin in or shelter them are closed off so far as reasonably practicable.
Where vermin have been detected, a continuing and effective extermination program is in place.

sections.title: Potable and nonpotable water
items: Potable water is available for drinking, washing, cooking, food and utensil washing, and personal service rooms.
Dispensers are clean, can be closed and have a tap.
No barrels, pails or tanks from which drinking water is dipped or poured, covered or not.
No common drinking cup or other common utensils in use.
Every nonpotable outlet is posted or marked as unsafe and not for drinking, washing or cooking.
Nonpotable systems are built so nothing can backflow or backsiphon into the potable supply.
Nonpotable water is not used to wash people, cooking or eating utensils, or clothing.

sections.title: Toilet facilities
items: For each sex, the water closet count meets Table J-1 for the most employees of that sex present at one time on a regular shift.
Toilet rooms are separate for each sex, or are single-occupancy rooms that lock from the inside and contain at least one water closet.
Each water closet is in its own compartment with a door and partitions high enough for privacy.
No leaks, overflows or backups from the sewage disposal method that could endanger employees.
Where this exception is relied on, transportation to nearby compliant toilet facilities is immediately available.

sections.title: Washing facilities and showers
items: Sinks and washrooms are clean and sanitary.
Lavatories are available to employees at the workplace.
Each lavatory runs hot and cold water, or tepid water.
Hand soap or a similar cleansing agent is stocked at the lavatories.
Individual cloth or paper towels, air blowers, or clean continuous cloth toweling are stocked and working near the lavatories.
If showers are required by another standard: one shower for each 10 employees of each sex, or fraction thereof, who must shower on the same shift.
Body soap or another cleansing agent is available near the showers.
Showers have hot and cold water feeding a common discharge line.
Each employee using a shower gets an individual clean towel.

sections.title: Change rooms, clothes drying, eating areas and food
items: Where protective clothing is required by another standard because of possible toxic contamination, change rooms have storage for street clothes and separate storage for protective clothing.
Employer-provided work clothes that get wet or are washed between shifts are dry before reuse.
No one eats or drinks in toilet rooms or in areas exposed to a toxic material.
Food waste receptacles are smooth, corrosion resistant and easily cleanable, or disposable.
Receptacles in use are emptied at least once each working day and are not overfilled.
Receptacles have a solid lid that fits tightly, unless they stay sanitary without one.
No food or beverages stored in toilet rooms or in areas exposed to a toxic material.
Where food service is provided, food is wholesome, free from spoilage and stored and handled so it is protected from contamination.

references: 29 CFR 1910.141: Sanitation (Part 1910 Subpart J, General Environmental Controls)
